how_it_works.title: How Paprika Works
how_it_works.description: Paprika is a unified research tool that connects you to the world’s academic papers by bridging multiple open-source databases.
how_it_works.content_1: Instead of relying on a single library, Paprika runs massive parallel queries against the world's largest open-access graphs, such as OpenAlex and Crossref, combining their results seamlessly.
how_it_works.content_2: Every academic API has completely different structures. We clean up and normalize these differences behind the scenes, presenting each paper in a clear, universal design—complete with citations, abstract, authors, and open-access status.
how_it_works.content_3: We don’t just use keyword matching. By leveraging advanced semantic relevance scores (via algorithms like OpenAlex), Paprika strives to present the most significant and relevant findings first.

what_changed.title: What Changed? — Release Timeline
what_changed.description: Step-by-step timeline of all Paprika features and major release milestones:

steps.title: Citation Engine & Release Timeline
changes: Added interactive citation generator modal supporting BibTeX, APA, MLA, IEEE, and Chicago.
Expanded bilingual (TR/EN) i18n support for all new modals and actions.

steps.title: Multi-Source & Localization Upgrade
changes: Built dual-source engine querying Crossref and OpenAlex open-access graphs simultaneously.
Added zero-flicker client-side locale detector with full English & Turkish translations.
Introduced calendar date-range filtering and relevance sorting.
Resolved Next.js 15 App Router & Turbopack build and ESLint issues.

steps.title: UI Refinements & Security Cleanup
changes: Enhanced button loading states across search and action workflows.
Cleaned up iframe embedding and redirect rules for improved security.

steps.title: Initial Launch & Core Architecture
changes: Launched the initial version of Paprika academic search engine.
Implemented Unified Article Cards, pagination, and detailed metadata modal.
Added dark mode support and Progressive Web App (PWA) installation features.
